body:
The session widened the driver's send confirmation: a submitted prompt now matches the driver's typed text when it is equal, or when it is non-empty and equals the typed text with a trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR or LF removed (the whitespace the CLI trims at submit); that trailing-only set is PROVISIONAL, awaiting the founder's word.
A send whose text ends in such whitespace is now confirmed and read back as the driver's own, the wheel stays with the driver, and a refused character is still refused; a prompt trimmed at the start claims nothing and the wheel goes to the human.
It closed the readiness-gate turn race: after the gate reads ready, the human-typing and turn-running checks, the link record, the send-issued line and the paste run under one lock, and hook events decide the claim, the session start, the turn start and end and the unsent-human wheel move under that same lock; a turn the wrapper learns of before the paste refuses turn-running with nothing typed.
A human key never takes that lock: the stdin path is untouched and human keystrokes never wait on a send.
The test-only fake agent gained an argv flag that trims the end of the prompt it submits.
No refusal word, event kind, exit code, CLI output line, config key, IPC method or crate was added or retired; the residual hook-latency window (a turn the CLI starts whose submit has not reached the wrapper before the paste) stays open, owned by the standing live rig.

body: The critical path confirmed send and readback: a driver's send whose text ends in trailing whitespace the CLI trims is now confirmed and read back rather than failing the exact match; the match is exact equality or the typed text less a trailing ASCII space, TAB, CR or LF run.

The critical path human takes the wheel: a prompt trimmed at the start, or differing in any other way, still claims nothing and the wheel goes to the human; the unsent-human wheel move is now decided under the send's flight lock.

Human keystrokes never blocked and human key takes the wheel: the new flight lock is never taken by a human key; the stdin path is unchanged, so these hold, re-asserted by the gate-wait human-key cases.

Send refused while the human types: the post-gate human-typing check now runs under the flight lock held across the link, send-issued and the paste; the refusal order and words are unchanged and nothing is typed on a refusal.
Any row stating the send confirmation or the readback is an exact match of the typed text is now stale: the claim tolerates the trailing trimmed run.

The viola send refusals (input-not-ready, no-prompt-submitted, turn-running, human-typing): no word, exit code or layout changed, but a turn the wrapper knows of before the paste now always refuses turn-running with no link and no send-issued.

Boundary tests sequenced on records and the boundary check never inspecting claude content: the fake agent that stands in for claude gains the argv-only flag --trim-prompt-end; it reads no env and the drift contract and recorded fixtures stay byte for byte.
Time bounds fall on the driver only: the send's confirmation window still waits with the lock released, so no new bound falls on the human.
Live readings never gate: no live claude start this session; the CLI's trimmed whitespace set stays an assumption, its live reading carried to the standing live rig.
A11y assertions inside existing suites and a11y failures are nextest failures: the new send, relabel, hook and CLI send cases run inside the existing nextest suites with no separate a11y driver.
CLI output rows — the list board, its captions, colour and SGR rules, truncation, the --help rows, wait and verify lines: no printed line or escape sequence changed.
Refusal and fault formats — unable and hint lines, code words, --json failure and refusal documents, exit codes, the unknown refusal: no refusal word, hint or exit code added or moved.

TUI passthrough terminal-byte rows — zero viola bytes on the terminal, focus, mouse and resize sequences, vendor content, the vt100 feed panic, run diagnostics: the paste and stdin paths emit nothing new to the terminal.
Revive, link and unlink, plugin install, frame verb, MCP tool and socket-directory or strict-modes refusal rows: the session reached none of those commands.

CI integration, SLO and budget rows, the screen-reader targets, manual passes and the absences (web frontend, touch, i18n, user time limit): no CI step, gate, threshold or tool changed and no capability was added or removed.

The delivery-confirmation claim now matches a driver's send when the submitted prompt equals the typed text exactly, or is non-empty and equals the typed text with its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF removed; leading or inner differences still claim nothing. The trim set is an assumption and the trailing-only side is PROVISIONAL, the founder's word owed.
The relabel still writes origin driver alone and the prompt-submitted line keeps the submitted text; no event kind, refusal word, event field, snapshot field, config key, IPC method, env var, crate or dependency was added.
The readiness-gate turn race is closed by a lock: after the gate returns ready, the human-typing and turn-running reads, the link record, send-issued and the paste run under one flight lock, and the wrapper decides the claim, the session-start claim, turn start and end and the unsent-human wheel move under that same lock; refusal order unchanged, a human key takes no flight lock.
A residual stays: a turn the CLI has started whose UserPromptSubmit has not reached the wrapper before the paste is beyond reach (hook latency unmeasured), carried to the standing live rig with a screen model.
The test-only fake agent gains an argv flag --trim-prompt-end that trims the trailing whitespace run from its UserPromptSubmit prompt; argv only, no env read.

body:
The send's delivery-confirmation claim no longer needs exact equality. It takes the submitted prompt when it equals the typed text, or when it is non-empty and equals the typed text with a trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR or LF removed. The tolerance is PROVISIONAL, a boundary widening that is escalated and still waits for the founder's word.
A driver's send whose text ends in whitespace the CLI trims is now relabelled driver and confirmed. It keeps the wheel, a refused character is still refused, and the relabel still writes origin alone and keeps the submitted text.
The readiness-gate turn race is closed by a lock. After the gate returns ready, the human-typing and turn-running reads, the implicit link record, send-issued and the paste all run under one flight lock. A turn whose prompt-submitted reaches the wrapper first refuses turn-running: nothing typed, no link, no send-issued. The confirmation window waits with the lock released.
The hook-event path makes the claim, the session-start claim, the turn start and end and the unsent-human wheel move under that one flight lock. The test-only fake agent gains the argv-only flag --trim-prompt-end.
No event kind, log line, log field, detail word, refusal word, IPC method, env var, config key or crate was added. The send-issued, send-confirmed and send-refused lines are unchanged, and no text is logged.
A residual stays open: a turn the CLI started whose UserPromptSubmit has not reached the wrapper before the paste is beyond reach, because hook latency is unmeasured.

the wrapper side of send in viola run, which runs the readiness gate, the refusal order (human-typing, turn-running), the implicit link record, send-issued, the paste and the confirmation window
the driver relabel of a hook event, which marks a confirmed send's prompt-submitted origin driver
test helpers for the send path's unit tests
the test-only fake agent that stands in for claude in CI, with its argv-only options and its UserPromptSubmit payload
the fake agent's argv option parse tests
the booted integration tests of viola send against the fake agent

body: A row that says the send-confirmed line or a confirmed send follows an exact match of the prompt to the typed text is stale. The match now also accepts the typed text with a trailing ASCII whitespace run removed, PROVISIONAL.
The unconfirmable send on the send line: a driver send whose text ends in whitespace the CLI trims is now confirmed and logs send-confirmed, where before it went unconfirmed.

The wrapper send-refused turn-running detail: it now also covers a turn whose prompt-submitted arrives after the readiness gate but before the paste. In that case no send-issued line and no link record are written.

The send path log events order and the implicit-link-before-send-issued event order: the order is unchanged, but the link record, send-issued and the paste now run under one flight lock held after the gate.
